title: Baby Talk
cn: 第 6 集 · 宝贝话题
novel: Marshall and Lily [[decided|decide]] it was time to have a baby. They began to [[research|research]] how to conceive a child with the gender of their choice. Marshall read books about diet and timing while Lily [[created|create]] charts and spreadsheets. They were so [[determined|determine]] that they turned their bedroom into a science [[laboratory|laboratory]]. Meanwhile, Robin was [[irritated|irritate]] by her new co-anchor, Becky. Becky was [[perky|perky]] and spoke in a baby voice that the audience seemed to love. Robin found it [[unprofessional|unprofessional]] and complained to the producers, but they told her that Becky's style was [[boosting|boost]] the ratings. Robin felt [[jealous|jealous]] and [[frustrated|frustrate]] at the same time. She had worked hard to be taken seriously as a journalist, and now a woman who talked like a child was getting more [[attention|attention]] than her. Barney tried to [[cheer|cheer]] Robin up by taking her to a sports bar, but it did not help. Back at the apartment, Marshall and Lily's baby plans hit a [[snag|snag]]. They realized that no method was [[guaranteed|guarantee]] to work and that nature would ultimately make the decision. They felt [[disappointed|disappoint]] but also [[relieved|relief]] because the pressure was off. They agreed to just let things happen [[naturally|naturally]]. Ted watched his friends navigate their challenges and thought about his own future. He wondered if he would ever find someone to start a family with. The episode ended with Robin [[confronting|confront]] Becky, who turned out to be much smarter than she [[appeared|appear]]. They actually had a [[genuine|genuine]] conversation and found some common ground.

decide.en: to make a choice about something

research.en: to study something to learn new facts

create.en: to make something new that did not exist

determine.en: to firmly decide to do something

laboratory.en: a room used for scientific research

jealous.en: feeling unhappy because someone has what you want

frustrate.en: to make someone feel blocked or upset

attention.en: interest or care given to something

snag.en: a small problem that delays something

disappoint.en: to make someone feel sad by not meeting hopes

relief.en: feeling better after worry goes away

naturally.en: in a way that is normal and expected

confront.en: to deal with a problem directly

appear.en: to seem or look a certain way
